On 30 October 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE]. The Council extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. It expressed willingness to work with Colombia's Government on further extension based on inter-party agreement [OPERATIVE]. Resolution 2694 already authorized monitoring of the Government–ELN ceasefire [ADDITIONAL]. The Council indicated willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification only when the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate protocols, noting the Secretary-General's update on resolution 2694 implementation [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil's representative, speaking for the Government of Colombia, stated the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will and supported the Government's total peace strategy [BRAZIL]. He hoped the Council could authorize EMC verification when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. The African members, speaking through Ghana, welcomed the unanimous mandate extension [A3]. They supported prospective EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions [A3]. Additionally, they pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people [A3]. colombia-structured-chair.short_separate_scopes:
On 30 October 2023, the Council voted unanimously (15 in favour) to adopt United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE].

The resolution extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024, maintaining existing authority for Government–ELN ceasefire monitoring and verification [OPERATIVE, ADDITIONAL].

Brazil's representative, speaking for Brazil, stated the Council should respond to Colombia's Government priorities and hoped to authorize EMC verification when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL].

Ghana, representing the three African members, welcomed the extension and supported prospective EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's confirmation of a ceasefire [A3].

The African members separately pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people [A3].

While both delegations supported future EMC consideration, resolution 2704 did not grant that authority, leaving it to the Secretary-General's update on implementation [ADDITIONAL].
